passage:
First Monday. Joseph skipped Saturday football and said, "The people outside my group are asleep." Anjali kept her voice warm. "What do you like about it? I'd like to understand." Joseph talked for an hour, glowing.
Two weeks later. Joseph stopped answering messages and left the class chat. Anjali noticed Joseph no longer ate with the cousins either. She waited at the gate and said, "I miss you. You don't have to explain anything." Joseph gave a small nod and left.
That Friday, Anjali told the school counsellor everything, including how Joseph had been cut off from everyone. It felt like a risk to the friendship, but Anjali stayed beside Joseph at the counsellor's door.

qa.q: What did Joseph stop doing on the first Monday?
What was Anjali feeling by the final scene, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Anjali felt worried but loyal; telling the counsellor, even though it felt like a risk, and staying beside Joseph at the door show it. 🤍

qa.q: Why did Anjali tell an adult even though Joseph might be upset?
qa.a: Joseph had been cut off from friends and cousins and had gone silent, so a trusted adult was needed; friendship alone was not enough.

qa.q: How might Joseph see Anjali's warm questions?
qa.a: Possibly as care rather than mockery, though Joseph still pulled away, so Anjali cannot be sure how it landed.

grounding: A friend changes after being pulled into an extreme online group; Anjali stays warm, asks questions and involves a counsellor when Joseph is cut off.

passage:
Week one. Sarika noticed Thomas had stopped coming to cricket. At lunch he talked about a new online group that "told the truth" about certain communities, and used words for them he'd never used before. Sarika wanted to say, "That's disgusting." Instead she asked, "Where are you reading this?" He showed her the forum. She didn't laugh.

Week two. Thomas was up till three most nights. He'd dropped his other friends. Sarika still sat with him. "You seem angry all the time now. Are you okay?" He shrugged. "At least they get me."

Week three. On Friday Thomas told her the group was holding a secret "training camp" on Sunday and had told him not to tell his parents, who "wouldn't understand." Sarika's stomach dropped. "Thomas, I care about you. I can't keep this."

She went to the school counsellor that afternoon and told her mother too. By evening, the counsellor had called Thomas's parents, who kept him home and reported the group. Thomas was angry. Sarika kept texting him anyway.

qa.q: When was the group's secret camp to be held?
qa.a: The camp was to be held on Sunday.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling when Thomas mentioned the secret camp?
qa.a: Sarika felt frightened for Thomas, her stomach dropping, because he was being cut off and could be at risk.

qa.q: What did Sarika do right across the three weeks?
qa.a: Sarika stayed his friend, asked warm questions instead of mocking, and told the counsellor and her mother the same day she learned of the secret camp.

qa.q: How might Thomas feel about Sarika now?
qa.a: Thomas feels angry and perhaps betrayed, but her continued texts may later help him see she acted out of care.

grounding: It shows a teen whose friend is pulled into an extreme online group, staying his friend, asking with warmth, and involving trusted adults the same day when he is cut off and at risk.

passage:
Ishita, you're worried about your friend and that group online? Sit. Let your Ganga Masi tell you something from when I was sixteen.

My closest friend then was Pinky. We did everything together. Then she found a chat forum, some group that said people like her were being wronged by people like our neighbours. Within months she changed. She stopped laughing at my jokes. She called our old friends traitors.

I wanted to shout at her. I wanted to mock the forum. But my mother said, "If you mock it, you push her further in." So I kept walking home with her. I asked her what she read and why it mattered. I listened more than I argued.

Then one evening she said the group wanted her to leave home and "join them properly." That night I told my mother everything. My mother went to Pinky's mother the same night.

It was hard. Pinky didn't speak to me for months. But she came back. Friendship and a trusted adult, together, that's what did it.

qa.q: What did Pinky call her old friends?
What was young Ganga feeling as Pinky changed?
qa.a: Ganga felt hurt and frustrated, wanting to shout and mock the forum, but also deeply worried about losing her friend.

qa.q: What was the key choice in Ganga Masi's story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Telling her mother the same night Pinky spoke of leaving home was key, because a trusted adult could protect Pinky while Ganga stayed her friend.

qa.q: What was it like for Pinky's mother to hear the news?
qa.a: Pinky's mother was likely shocked and frightened, but able to act that night because Ganga's mother came to her.

grounding: It shows an elder recalling a friend pulled into an extreme online group, staying her friend, asking with warmth and involving a trusted adult when the friend was at risk.
